gaps.fact: The Grande Montagne de Reims by that name: the Codex teaches the Montagne de Reims and its north facing Grand Cru villages but never uses the Court's term.
Chardonnay is about 30 per cent of the plantings: no chapter, article or question gives any share of the vineyard.
Pinot Noir is about 38 per cent and Meunier about 32 per cent of the plantings: the Codex says which district each grape leads but never how much of the vineyard each holds.

The full contents of the liqueur de tirage: the Codex gives wine, sugar (about 24 grams a litre) and yeast, but never the yeast nutrient and the riddling aid (bentonite or alginate) that go in with them.

The Comité Interprofessionnel du Vin de Champagne, the growers' and houses' joint body: it appears only as a wrong option in the Wine Law stem i-sf6m8ep4 and in a temperatures note; nothing says what it is or does.
Grandes Marques, the term for the great houses: it occurs in no chapter, article, card or question.

Three grower producers and three houses outside the Grandes Marques: the article names Jacques Selosse, Egly-Ouriet, Larmandier-Bernier and Pierre Péters as growers and Drappier, Gosset and Philipponnat among the smaller houses, but no question of either bank asks a grower by name.
The best Champagne vintages of the last fifteen years: the Codex holds no vintage list by house rule (nothing volatile).

courtUpdates.now: The Champagne specification homologated by the ministerial order of 31 July 2025 (Bulletin officiel of 7 August 2025) recognises Chardonnay rose as an eighth principal variety beside Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Arbane and Petit Meslier, and admits the disease resistant Voltis on adaptation terms, at no more than 10 per cent of a blend. The Codex article (grapes; made, viticulture; exam) already carries both.
courtUpdates.source: info.agriculture.gouv.fr, Bulletin officiel du ministère de l'Agriculture, cahier des charges AOC Champagne homologated 31 July 2025; WSET blog 2025, The grape varieties of Champagne; wein.plus, Voltis approved in Champagne.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 60 (Champagne), Village 35 (Champagne), 95 in all. Beyond the map, Producers & Icons asks nine Champagne houses, cuvées and sites (the Club Trésors among them), History & Figures three (the widow Clicquot, the Hautvillers cellarer, the riots of 1911), Food & Pairing two, Sparkling Wine World five on Champagne houses abroad and the name on American labels and Viticulture & Winemaking two (Cordon de Royat, 41B). The Introductory column is fully served, the method above all; the Certified column is strong on the tirage, the dosage, the crus, the label codes and the opening standards and thin on the planting shares, the Grande Montagne, the Comité Champagne, the words Grandes Marques and the grower roll. No factual error found: the press figures (4,000 kilograms, 2,550 litres, cuvée 2,050, taille 500), the dosage bands and the three gram tolerance, the 24 grams of tirage sugar, 17 Grand Cru and 42 Premier Cru villages, Chouilly at 100 for Chardonnay alone, the 1908, 1911 and 1927 Aube dates, Coteaux Champenois in 1974 and the 80 per cent cap on a vintage all hold. One reading to carry: the Court says grapes are picked earlier to preserve acidity, while the article warns that the aim is a balanced base wine rather than unripe fruit; give the Court's line on the paper. One search spent, on the July 2025 specification; a further revision adding resistant varieties is reported as pending and is not confirmed here.
